numerical_failure.observed_behavior: HDFStore.select with a "<" (or "<=") where-query on a datetime64/timedelta64 data column also returns rows whose value is NaT, because NaT is stored as iNaT (int64 min) which sorts below every real value. In the reproducer, store.select("t", where="col < '2020-01-01 00:00:01'")["pos"].tolist() returns [0, 2].
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Only the row with a real value below the bound should match; the NaT row should be excluded, giving [0]. The result should agree with the equivalent in-memory comparison, which never matches NaT for "<".
trigger_conditions: where-query uses "<" or "<=" against a datetime64 or timedelta64 data column in HDFStore.select
column contains NaT values stored as iNaT
column kind is datetime64 or timedelta64 (the guard is not applied to other kinds, e.g. PeriodDtype which reports kind 'integer')

numerical_characteristics.dtype: datetime64/timedelta64 columns stored as int64 with NaT encoded as iNaT
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: iNaT is the int64 minimum and sorts below every real value
category_specific_evidence: NaT in datetime64/timedelta64 columns is stored as iNaT (int64 min), which sorts below every real value, so an unguarded '<' or '<=' where-query matched the NaT rows.
BinOp.generate in pandas/core/computation/pytables.py now emits ((col != iNaT) & (col < val)) for '<'/'<=' when the column kind starts with datetime or timedelta; '>'/'>=' need no guard.

PR#68031 reproducer: DataFrame with col = to_datetime(['2020-01-01 00:00:00','2020-01-01 00:00:02',NaT]).as_unit('s') appended with data_columns=True, index=False; select where col < '2020-01-01 00:00:01' returns pos [0, 2] but [0] is wanted.
Added tests test_select_ordering_comparison_skips_nat cover datetime, datetime as unit 's', tz-aware UTC datetime, and timedelta columns with NaT, for ops <, <=, >, >=.
test_select_ordering_comparison_skips_nat_on_index covers a DatetimeIndex with NaT for '<' and '<='.

test_append_with_timedelta had expectations that encoded the old NaT-matching behaviour; its comment said 'we don't really deal with the NaT properly', and its expectations were changed to in-memory comparisons.
reproduction_risks: The old test_append_with_timedelta expectations matched NaT rows, so a reproduction relying on them will differ from the fixed behaviour.
The guard applies only when the column kind starts with datetime or timedelta, so non-datetime columns are not cov
